lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice comparing everyday options with comparatives and superlatives.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Two colleagues choose between lunch places, cafés, routes, or weekend activities.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Comparing options and explaining a preference.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik compare two or three everyday options and choose the one that fits best.

main_focus.name: comparatives and superlatives for choices
main_focus.description: Use forms like bättre, billigare, närmare, and bäst to compare practical options.
model_examples: Den andra lunchen är billigare, men den här är bäst.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use comparative or superlative forms naturally 4-5 times in the dialogue.

useful_chunks: Det beror på vad vi vill göra.
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use concrete adjectives that fit food, cafés, routes, and simple plans.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person suggests choosing between two or three options.
dialogue_shape.middle: They compare practical qualities like distance, price, taste, or time.
dialogue_shape.ending: They choose one option and give a simple reason.

target_complexity.repetition: multiple comparative examples should appear naturally

focus: which qualities make one option preferable
which option is chosen and why

sentence_focus: one sentence with billigare or dyrare
one sentence with närmare or snabbare
one sentence explaining a preference between two options
